item.title: Jazz, TX Presents: Jazzmeia Horn – Wed, Oct 28 (SOLD OUT)
item.description:
Showtimes: 07:30 PM (SOLD OUT)

Jazzmeia Horn brings a powerful, expressive voice to the world of modern jazz. Drawing on her gospel roots, she explores themes of love and social change through her music. She has won both the 2013 Sarah Vaughan International Jazz Vocal Competition and the 2015 Thelonious Monk International Jazz Competition.

Born in Dallas and raised in a church-going family, Ms. Horn studied at Booker T. Washington High School for the Performing and Visual Arts and The New School in New York City. Her debut album, "A Social Call," earned a Grammy nomination, and "Love and Liberation" earned another. Today she tours the world and teaches through The Jazz Horn International Vocal Initiative.

As always, our kitchen and bar will be open for dinner service.

See you at the show!

item.title: "The Best is Yet to Come" - A Tribute to Frank Sinatra with Wyatt Michael and the Jazz, TX House Band – Thu, Oct 29
item.description:
Showtimes: 07:00 PM, 09:30 PM

Jazz, TX brings back our favorite vocal phenom Wyatt Michael, best know for his performance of "Mack the Knife" on season 21 of The Voice.

Backed by the Jazz, TX House Band, Wyatt pays tribute to all the classic Sinatra hits like "You Make Me Feel So Young," "Fly Me To The Moon," "Pennies From Heaven," and many others.

More about Wyatt Michael:

From a young age, Wyatt Michael studied the piano and while he never connected with the instrument as a child, his appreciation for music was instilled. Wyatt began writing music with his brother and over the next few years, they began performing their original music in the rock band Chasing Avenir. As Chasing Avenir released their first EP “Blue” and played at the National Theater in Richmond, VA, Wyatt was introduced to the jazz standards and immediately fell in love with them.

Once the decision was made to become a jazz singer, Wyatt joined forces with Chris Whiteman and began work on his first solo album “Renaissance.” Released on November 8th 2019, “Renaissance” is made up of songs written by David Mann, composer of the classic “In the Wee Small Hours of the Morning,” that have never before been released to the public. Wyatt was given special permission from Mann’s son and estate to bring these songs to life.

After only two years of full-time singing, Wyatt was featured on season 21 of “The Voice” where he turned the chairs of both Kelly Clarkson, and Ariana Grande during the Blind Auditions stage. Wherever Wyatt Michael performs, he brings the passion, emotion, and musicianship of the golden age of music—honoring the legacy of the giants who came before him and carrying it forward for generations to come.

As always, our kitchen and bar will be open for dinner service.

See you at the show!

item.title: Midnight Set with the Demetreis Thornton Quartet | “Swing Low” Jazz Bass Trombone – Fri, Oct 30
item.description:
Showtimes: 11:59 PM

Been to one of our regular shows? You know the drill: great sets, dinner service, a polished room. Midnight, that goes out the window.

The Midnight Set is jazz unplugged: looser, louder, no rules. Late-night bites, strong drinks, good company, and the kind of playing that only comes out after hours.

This set it's bass trombonist Demetreis Thornton, out of El Paso and one of the sharpest young voices coming up today. His sound pulls from Curtis Fuller, Steve Davis, Benny Golson, Slide Hampton, and Art Blakey, and he's already shared stages with heavyweights like Gary Smulyan, Andre Hayward, Brad Leali, and Mike Sailors. Since landing in Austin in 2023, he's been everywhere, composing, arranging, teaching, and playing across Central Texas.

Tonight he brings "Swing Low," his showcase for an instrument most bands treat as "trombone 4." Demetreis treats it as a lead voice: songbook standards, hard bop, and ballads, all filtered through a sound that's entirely his own. See you at midnight.

The kitchen will be offering our late night menu and the bar will be fully be open for drink service!

item.title: The Hot Club of Cowtown – Tue, Nov 03
item.description:
Showtimes: 07:30 PM

Whit Smith's guitar and Elana James's fiddle argue and agree in the same breath. That argument is the sound of Hot Club of Cowtown: old hot jazz braided into Texas swing.

The Austin trio just joined the International Western Music Hall of Fame, on top of a Texas Western Swing Hall of Fame honor and fifteen albums. Their album Limelight hits CD this month after a run as a digital-only release in 2025. Hear a Django Reinhardt lick land next to a Bob Wills fiddle break, from three players who have carried this sound from the Grand Ole Opry to Fuji Rock.

item.description:

Jim Snidero once stood inside John Coltrane's old house on Long Island. He wrote a new album about that day. It's called House of Trane , and he brings it to Jazz, TX. Snidero has a Grammy and a sound critics call rare. He backed Frank Sinatra on record, played in the Mingus Big Band, and got his start on the road with organist Brother Jack McDuff. In 2024, Downbeat's critics named him a top five alto sax player. Jim will be joined by Stefan Karlsson on piano, Unonna Okegwo on bass, and Jason Tiemann on drums as he leads the group through the new album and a career of standards.

This quintet does the same thing on purpose, one tune swinging, the next one loose and electric. Stick around after the last song.

From tender Christmas ballads to swinging blues and festive bossa rhythms, it’s a joyful celebration you won’t want to miss.

As always our kitchen and bar will be open for dinner service.

Merry Christmas and see you at the show!

item.title: Christmas, After Hours with Diego Martinez and Fermata Jazz – Sat, Dec 26
item.description:
Showtimes: 11:59 PM

Been to one of our regular shows? You know the drill: great sets, dinner service, a polished room. Midnight, that goes out the window. The Midnight Set is jazz unplugged: looser, louder, no rules. Late-night bites, strong drinks, good company, and the kind of playing that only comes out after hours.

Celebrate the magic of the season as Fermata Jazz takes the stage with San Antonio natives Diego Martinez, Chris Vu, and Dylan Knowles leading the way. The group brings holiday cheer with swinging arrangements, tender ballads, and jazzy takes on your favorite Christmas classics. From the Rat Pack charm of “Let It Snow” to the nostalgic warmth of “Have Yourself a Merry Little Christmas,” this late-night performance captures the joyful spirit of the season.

***Your $35 ticket includes one complimentary craft cocktail or beverage from our menu (a $15 value). The kitchen will be offering our late night menu and the bar will be fully open for drink service.

Merry Christmas and see you at midnight!

item.title: With a Little Help from Our Friends: The Music of the Beatles – Tue, Dec 29
item.description:

Adam Carrillo, Brandon Guerra, Mike Porter, and Chris Vu turn Jazz, TX into a Beatles room for the night. Carrillo plays sax, Vu plays piano, Porter holds down bass, and Guerra plays drums and runs the show on the mic. Expect songs like "Day Tripper," "Come Together," and "All You Need Is Love," worked the way a jazz quartet works a standard.

As always, our kitchen and bar are open for dinner service.

See you at the show!

A Jazz, TX tradition! The dance floor is always open for Salsa Night with Jose Amador and NATIAO Latin Jazz. Since our Grand Opening in 2016, Jazz, TX has been proud to feature monthly Salsa nights with the best Salsa band in town!

item.title: Jazz, TX Presents: Sammy Miller and the Congregation! – Thu, Jan 07
item.description:
Showtimes: 07:00 PM, 09:30 PM

Get ready! Jazz, TX audience favorite Sammy Miller and the Congregation returns to San Antonio! If you've never seen their show, you're in for a treat ... and a wild ride!

Sammy Miller and The Congregation are on a mission to put the generosity back into jazz and bring art back to the people. Juilliard trained and drummer on a Grammy® nominated album, Sammy Miller has been hailed as "the perfect player scholar” (The Wall Street Journal)

Miller has spent the last decade making jazz accessible to a new generation of listeners and learners. From Lincoln Center to The White House, TEDx to The Newport Jazz Festival, with special guests including Jon Batiste and Wynton Marsalis, Miller’s band, Sammy Miller and The Congregation, has headlined the most prominent Jazz festivals for over a decade. The Congregation specializes in joyful jazz – music that feels good. They recently released the album, Joyful Jazz at Lincoln Center (2023).

After working with over 60,000 students in 45 states, Miller launched the music education platform PLAYBOOK (www.thisisplaybook.com) to offer teachers the tools to inspire lifelong musicians. Miller recently discussed his music education philosophy in his New York Times op-ed titled “We’re Teaching Music to Kids All Wrong”.

As always, our kitchen and bar are open for service.

See you at the show!
